newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand dollar ends firmly, touches 68 on TWI.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand dollar ends firmly, touches 68 on TWI.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended stronger on Monday and dealers said its Trade-Weighted Index was approaching levels that may cause headaches for Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash.
The Kiwi closed at US$0.7084/91 and 68.00 on the TWI, up from 0.7068/75 and 67.81 at the opening and having traded a 0.7073-89 range on the day.

"We're starting the New Year proper with, again, a good performance by the currency in the light of what is a very strong U.S. dollar and an Aussie which, while it's not weakening much below US$0.7900 the figure, still looks quite soft," a

There was good offshore investor demand for the currency and strong talk of further Eurokiwi issues, with New Zealand interest rates still attractive despite falling substantially over the past several months, he said.

Despite some profit-taking around the US$0.7090 area, there were prospects of a test of 71 cents and then up to around 0.7120. The Kiwi also looked set to perform strongly on the Australian dollar cross.
Another dealer said Aussie reaction to weak current account data had been muted, and the main feature of the market was the strength of the U.S. dollar.

"We've seen a TWI at 68 the figure which is equivalent to last year's highs, and if this dollar strength continues, Dr Brash is going to have some TWI conditions much stronger than anticipated," he said.

"That'll be interesting because then he's going to have interest rates go down again and that's going to reignite the housing market and we're going to be in all sorts of problems again...At the moment I would say the key to this is the

Brash said at the time of last month's Monetary Policy Statement that he was comfortable with a combination of 90-day rates around 8.5 percent and the TWI at 66.5. Ninety-day rates ended on Monday at 7.83 percent.
